legal_status_note: Synthetic training cases. Penalty figures are statutory ceilings, not predictions or automatic penalties. Confirm commencement and current Gazette text before legal use.

cases.title: Healthcare Patient Data Breach
cases.scenario_background: A digital clinic stores patient profiles, prescriptions and appointment records in cloud infrastructure. A compromised privileged credential exports a large dataset. MFA is absent for the affected account and central access logs are incomplete.
facts: Patient records were accessible through a privileged account.
MFA was absent for the affected account.
Central monitoring did not capture all database access.
A processor supported the cloud environment under contract.
The organisation must establish the incident timeline before deciding statutory notifications.
legal_issues: Section 8(1): Data Fiduciary responsibility for processing undertaken by it or on its behalf.
Rule 6: notified security safeguard categories, subject to commencement.
penalty_analysis: Potentially relevant only if the statutory contravention is established and the provision is operative; not an automatic fine.
Separate analysis if required intimation is not made in the prescribed manner/timing once applicable.
remediation: Contain the compromised credential and preserve forensic evidence.
Enable strong authentication and privileged-access controls.
Centralise access logging and monitor anomalous exports.
Review processor security obligations and assurance.
Run a documented breach assessment and notification workflow.
Test restoration and incident-response playbooks.

cases.title: E-commerce Consent Withdrawal
cases.scenario_background: An online marketplace collects an email address and phone number for account creation and separately asks for marketing consent. A customer withdraws marketing consent, but a CRM integration continues promotional messages for several weeks.
facts: Account and marketing purposes were separated.
Withdrawal was available in account settings.
The CRM retained a stale marketing-consent state.
The organisation did not test withdrawal propagation end to end.
legal_issues: Section 8: Data Fiduciary accountability and processor governance.
Rule 3: detailed notice requirements, subject to commencement.
Rule 14: operational rights mechanisms, subject to commencement.
penalty_analysis: Requires identification of the exact contravention and commencement status; not a penalty prediction.
remediation: Create purpose-specific consent identifiers.
Propagate withdrawal events to CRM and marketing processors.
Add suppression checks before every campaign send.
Retain versioned consent and withdrawal evidence.
Test withdrawal across every downstream system.

cases.title: Fintech Cross-border Processing Review
cases.scenario_background: A fintech uses an Indian production database but permits an overseas support team to access customer profiles. Backups also replicate to a foreign region. Procurement recorded the vendor but not remote-access or backup destinations.
facts: Primary production storage is in India.
Overseas support personnel can access customer records.
Backups replicate to a foreign region.
Sector-specific regulatory obligations may also apply.
legal_issues: Section 16: transfers outside India and Central Government restrictions.
Rule 15: transfer framework, subject to commencement.
Section 8: Data Fiduciary responsibility and security safeguards.
penalty_analysis: Do not infer a penalty merely from an overseas destination; establish the operative restriction and facts first.
remediation: Inventory remote access and backup destinations.
Map processors and subprocessors.
Apply least privilege and just-in-time support access.
Review applicable transfer restrictions and sector rules.
Update contracts and the transfer register.
Reassess architecture after vendor changes.

cases.title: EdTech Children's Data Profiling
cases.scenario_background: An education platform identifies users under 18 and stores learning behaviour. A marketing SDK profiles activity for targeted advertising, while the product team has not implemented the applicable verifiable-consent workflow or documented an exemption analysis.
facts: The service is directed at students and collects learning activity.
The platform can identify users below 18.
A marketing SDK receives behavioural events.
legal_issues: Section 9: additional obligations relating to children's personal data.
Rules 10-12: verifiable consent and specified exemptions, subject to commencement.
penalty_analysis: A ceiling only. Establish the precise contravention, applicability, commencement and evidence before any enforcement conclusion.
remediation: Disable inappropriate child profiling/advertising paths pending legal review.
Implement the applicable verifiable-consent workflow.
Review marketing SDK data flows and processor terms.
Document any qualifying exemption and its conditions.
Restrict access and retain verification evidence.
